subject.title: fix(agents): bound finished bash process session retention

question: Should completed background-process poll/log records be allowed to evict before the existing job TTL when fixed memory budgets are exceeded?
rationale: The implementation is intentionally bounded and proven, but it unconditionally changes the retention behavior for existing delayed polls; code review cannot determine the desired product contract alone.

options.title: Accept bounded early eviction
options.body: Approve the 50-session and 2,000,000-character budgets as the new retention policy, accepting that oldest completed records can expire before TTL under burst load.

options.title: Preserve TTL availability
options.body: Require a revised design that keeps completed poll/log records available through TTL or introduce an explicitly approved compatibility policy before changing the default.

options.title: Pause for contract design
options.body: Defer this PR until the intended delayed-poll and memory-budget contract is documented by the runtime owners.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded early eviction
recommendation.body: Approve the 50-session and 2,000,000-character budgets as the new retention policy, accepting that oldest completed records can expire before TTL under burst load.

likelyOwner.reason: liuy is the only named recent area contact in the supplied PR timeline and is the best available routing candidate for the agent-runtime contract choice.
